answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake bond that is forfeited when collusion is found. Each agent locks a bond sized to its claimed influence; a cluster of look-alike identities at a harbor that pools collateral is provably costly, because N masquerading agents need N fully slashable deposits, not one. A violet similarity graph flags near-duplicate behaviour, and every flagged member loses its bond to the honest minority that the atlas of attestations certifies, so faking volume costs more than it unlocks, and cost scales linearly with each alias minted.
